article.title: Hindi to English: Daily routine sentence
article.description: Hindi: 'मैं सुबह जल्दी उठता हूं और टहलने जाता हूं।' English: 'I wake up early in the morning and go for a walk.' Teaching point: Hindi often omits the subject pronoun context that English requires explicitly; also note 'जाता हूं' (habitual present) maps to English simple present, not present continuous.
article.content: Hindi: 'मैं सुबह जल्दी उठता हूं और टहलने जाता हूं।' English: 'I wake up early in the morning and go for a walk.' Teaching point: Hindi often omits the subject pronoun context that English requires explicitly; also note 'जाता हूं' (habitual present) maps to English simple present, not present continuous.

generated.caption:
Ever find yourself translating daily habits from Hindi? It's common to wonder which tense to use!

For regular, habitual actions in Hindi like 'जाता हूं', English uses the simple present tense. It's for things you do consistently!

So, 'मैं सुबह जल्दी उठता हूं और टहलने जाता हूं' becomes 'I wake up early in the morning and go for a walk.' Simple, right?

generated.script: Daily routine batate time ye mistake hoti hai na sabse? Dekho, jab hum apni daily routine batate hain na, toh Hindi mein hum 'mai' sometimes skip kar dete hain. Jaise, 'subah jaldi uthta hoon'. But English mein you *have* to use 'I'. So, 'I wake up early in the morning'. Aur 'jaata hoon' jaise habitual actions ke liye English mein hum simple present use karte hain, like 'go for a walk', not 'I am going'. Toh, 'मैं सुबह जल्दी उठता हूं और टहलने जाता हूं' ka correct translation hai 'I wake up early in the morning and go for a walk'. Toh ab yaad rahega na? Apni daily routine batate time 'I' use karna mat bhoolna, aur habitual actions ke liye always use simple present. Isiliye, 'I wake up early in the morning and go for a walk'. slides.headlineRest: — How to Translate This Hindi Sentence
slides.body: Let's learn to translate a common daily routine sentence from Hindi to English. Consider the Hindi sentence: 'मैं सुबह जल्दी उठता हूं और टहलने जाता हूं।' The correct English translation is: 'I wake up early in the morning and go for a walk.' Notice that while Hindi can sometimes imply the subject, English explicitly requires the subject pronoun 'I' here. Furthermore, 'जाता हूं' denotes a habitual action in Hindi, which accurately translates to the English simple present tense ('go'), not the present continuous.
